title: Fourteen Winters and One Short Crack
subtitle: 日常饮食 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 日常饮食（生活与学习·饮食与健康）
meta: 主题语境：日常饮食（生活与学习·饮食与健康）　|　核心词汇：egg　|　正文 343 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 egg 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1943 my grandmother ① boiled an egg that no guest in the house would have eaten, and she said the boiling was the whole of the winter. The ② egg, meaning the food and not the cell, ran fourteen winters and stayed unnamed in the book; an egg, she said, is the only thing in a house that is judged by how long it is left uneaten.

Every ③ egg in that house had the same short crack at the end of it, and the ④ egg at the end, meaning the one they kept for the child and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever thanked twice. An egg, my mother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to eat; my grandmother said the eating is the part that fills fourteen winters.

My uncle meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the egg was the whole of the story, meaning the cell and not the food. The ⑥ egg, meaning the cell and not any of that, is the only thing in a story that everybody speaks of and nobody sees; egg, he said, is either something you boil or the only word that means both a food and a cell. He said the cell is the part they remember.

By 1952 the ⑦ egg had become a line in a recipe, and the recipe had become an argument about the short crack. The ⑧ egg of the whole thing, my grandmother wrote in January, was one house and fourteen winters of eating; egg, she said, is either the one at the end or the reason you learned to eat. She said the eating was never mentioned.

The ⑨ egg I remember is the one named in the recipe, which was shared in 1964 and is still described as the quietest in the house. An ⑩ egg, my mother said in 1966, is the only one that improves by being eaten; every egg, she said, is a cell that has agreed to look like a food. She said the cell was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 蛋；鸡蛋（指那座房子里煮过的那一只）
B. n. 蛋；鸡蛋（指那只蛋本身，与卵细胞相对）
C. 固定搭配：boil an egg 煮一只蛋
D. n. 蛋；鸡蛋（指留给孩子的那一只）
E. n. 蛋；鸡蛋（抽象总称，指一家人的吃蛋之事）
F. n. 蛋；鸡蛋（指食谱上写到、被列名的那一种）
G. n. 卵；卵细胞（指故事里人人都讲却无人见过的那样东西）
H. n. 卵细胞（抽象总称，指人人都讲却无人见过的那种东西）

items.q: boiled an egg that no guest in the house would have eaten
The egg, meaning the food and not the cell
the egg was the whole of the story
the egg had become a line in a recipe
The egg of the whole thing
An egg, my mother said in 1966

answers.why: boil an egg 意为“煮一只蛋”，1943 年祖母煮了一只屋子里没有一位客人肯吃的蛋。
egg 意为“蛋、鸡蛋”，指那只蛋本身而不是卵细胞，它经过了十四个冬天而在簿子上没有名字。
egg 意为“蛋、鸡蛋”，指那座房子里的每一只蛋，每一只到头都有同一道短短的裂纹。
egg 意为“蛋、鸡蛋”，指留给孩子的那一只，是唯一有人谢过两次的。
egg 意为“卵、卵细胞”，指故事里人人都讲却无人见过的那样东西，叔叔说这枚卵就是那个故事的全部。
egg 意为“卵细胞”，指人人都讲却无人见过的那种东西而不是那只蛋，是故事里人人都讲、却无人见过的东西。
egg 意为“蛋、鸡蛋”，指食谱上写到、被列名的那一种，到 1952 年这只蛋成了食谱里的一行。
egg 意为“蛋、鸡蛋”，祖母一月写道，整件事的吃蛋之事是一座房子和十四个冬天的食用。
egg 意为“蛋、鸡蛋”，我记得的是食谱上列名的那一种，1964 年分着吃了，至今仍被说成屋子里最安静的一种。
egg 为抽象总称，母亲 1966 年说，一只蛋是唯一会因为被好好吃掉而变得更好的东西。

那只蛋，指的是那只蛋本身而不是卵细胞，经过了十四个冬天而在簿子上没有名字。（egg）

叔叔说这枚卵就是那个故事的全部，指的是卵而不是那只蛋。（egg）
